meta.name: Post FX rate change commentary to Slack with Frankfurter and Claude

name: Monitor an exchange rate and post Claude's commentary to Slack

parameters.content:
## FX rate monitor with AI commentary

On a schedule, this workflow checks an exchange rate via the free Frankfurter API (no API key required), compares it to the last checked rate, and — if it moved beyond a threshold you set (or on the very first run) — asks Claude to write a short, factual note about the move and posts it to Slack.

### Before you activate
1. Add an Anthropic API key as a credential in n8n (Credential type: Anthropic), and assign it in the "Call Claude (Anthropic) API" node.
2. Open the "Set: config" node and set your currency pair (`baseCurrency` / `targetCurrency`), your move threshold in percent (`thresholdPercent`), and your Slack Incoming Webhook URL (no Slack app/OAuth needed).
3. Adjust the Schedule Trigger to whatever check frequency you want (defaults to every 6 hours).

### Note on "significant move" detection
This uses n8n's workflow static data to remember the last checked rate, which is only persisted for automatically-triggered executions (not manual test runs) — the first manual test will always be treated as a first run and post a commentary.

Step 1 — Fetch & compare

On a schedule, fetches the current exchange rate from the Frankfurter API and compares it to the last checked rate (remembered via workflow static data), computing the percent change.

Step 2 — Write commentary

If the move is beyond your threshold (or this is the first check), asks Claude to write a short, factual, non-speculative note about the rate change — no predictions, no investment advice.

Step 3 — Deliver to Slack

Posts the commentary to Slack via an Incoming Webhook. Checks the actual response body (Slack returns the text "ok" on success) rather than just the absence of an error.

nodes.name: Set: config
nodes.notes: Placeholder values. Set your currency pair, move threshold, and your own Slack Incoming Webhook URL before activating.

nodes.name: Fetch exchange rate
nodes.notes: Frankfurter API (https://frankfurter.dev), ECB reference rates, no API key required. Confirmed live response shape via a real request, 2026-08-14: {"amount":1.0,"base":"USD","date":"...","rates":{"JPY":...}}.

nodes.name: Check for significant move
nodes.notes: Uses $getWorkflowStaticData('global') to remember the last checked rate across executions. Static data only persists for automatically-triggered executions (not manual test runs) — confirmed against docs.n8n.io, matching the same behavior already documented in PUB-002.

nodes.name: Move significant?
nodes.notes: True on the first run, or when the move exceeds thresholdPercent from "Set: config". False routes to the skip branch below with no Claude call and no Slack post.

nodes.name: Build Claude prompt
nodes.notes: Builds the system/user prompt sent to Claude. The system prompt instructs Claude to state facts only and never give investment/trading advice.

nodes.name: Call Claude (Anthropic) API
nodes.notes: No credential ID is embedded — assign your own Anthropic credential in n8n before activating.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { model: 'claude-sonnet-5', max_tokens: 512, system: $json.systemPrompt, messages: [ { role: 'user', content: $json.userPrompt } ] } }}

nodes.name: Build Slack message
nodes.notes: Extracts Claude's generated text and formats it into the Slack message body posted by the next node.

nodes.name: Slack post succeeded?
nodes.notes: Checks the response body equals "ok" (Slack's documented literal success response) rather than just the absence of a thrown error — an invalid webhook URL can return HTTP 200 with an unrelated page instead of a clean error (this exact failure mode was found and fixed in an earlier template, PUB-002).
